summary1: I am a software engineer who works like a forward-deployed engineer: embedded with the customer from discovery through a live system, and still close enough to the product to turn field friction into something reusable.
summary2: At Adatafy / Novaspect I have delivered about 10 industrial software implementations across pharma, food, campus utilities, biofuels, and chemicals. Sites are typically 30–150 users. I have owned discovery, solution design, configuration, integrations, UAT, go-live, training, and hypercare, including 4–5 concurrent projects at the busiest point.
summary3: The customer-facing work is solutions engineering and pre-sales as much as delivery. I run workshops with executives, IT, vendors, plant managers, and operators, give about 30–40 tailored demos a year, and turn messy workflows into architectures, user stories, and phased rollouts. Eight of ten customers I have led came back for a second phase or extra work.
summary4: I also build the product around the deployment. I led the client-side design and testing for the first Shiftconnector (Seqonis) to SAP PM integration and helped make it a reusable offering. I wrote the core of a one-click testing product for a Fortune 500 food manufacturer, now used at sites in the United States and Mexico. Python and PowerShell automation cut manual setup effort by up to 60%.
summary5: On the AI side I ship evidence-first agents, not open-ended chat. In the field that has meant LLM assistants for operators, with structured knowledge and guardrails. On my own, PharmaOps Copilot and Seller Ops Copilot answer from deterministic tools and evals before a model writes the narrative.
summary6: Earlier, at NVIDIA I built CloudXR demos and technical enablement for a medical-training partner, and at Dolby I rolled out Agile delivery that cut cross-team meetings and cycle time. I am looking for forward-deployed, solutions, product, and deployment roles where that mix is the job.
